To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
indistinguishability obfuscated RAM programs are as succinct as their input, and that indistinguishability garbled RAM programs are as space-efficient as their input.
indistinguishability obfuscated circuits can be garbled, and garbled RAM programs can be obfuscated.

(i) we can garble RAM programs in space and runtime that are the same as that of the input program; and (ii) we can obfuscate RAM programs with the same efficiency, at the cost of requiring the underlying primitives to be sub-exponential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between succinctness and obfuscation.
the following question. How much of the functionality of garbled RAM can be achieved without the overhead of storing the input program?
the following fundamental question: Can we garble programs that are larger than the space of the universe?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper is a great example of how to combine techniques to obtain new results in a field of cryptography that has been growing very rapidly in the last decade or two.
the paper is a significant contribution to the area of fully succinct garbling schemes.
we have constructed the first fully succinct Garbled RAM scheme, assuming the existence on one-way functions and iO, and that the size of the obfuscated program is sublinear in the size of the input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to combine two seemingly incompatible approaches for obfuscation: the deterministic fixed-prefix approach, and the randomized oblivious-RAM approach.
we show how to combine the techniques of KLW and CHJV to obtain fully succinct garbling.
we construct the first indistinguishability obfuscated RAM programs with succinctness, and that we do so with a simple and modular construction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of indistinguishability (or even one-way) obfuscation, we can construct obfuscation schemes that offer a level of security that is comparable to that of the underlying program, even when the program is very complex.
, in some sense, the indistinguishability obfus-cator for circuits is "universal" and can be applied to programs with different structures.
the efficiency of garbled RAM schemes can be improved dramatically, and that the efficiency of the garbled RAM scheme is not a limiting factor for the efficiency of the obfuscated programs.
